Please polish the following text to make it more eloquent and professional, keeping all original information unchanged:

For positive semidefinite matrices $A$ and $B$, Ando and Zhan proved the inequalities $||| f(A)+f(B) ||| \ge ||| f(A+B) |||$ and $||| g(A)+g(B) ||| \le ||| g(A+B) |||$, for any unitarily invariant norm, and for any non-negative operator monotone $f$ on $[0,\infty)$ with inverse function $g$. These inequalities have very recently been generalised to non-negative concave functions $f$ and non-negative convex functions $g$, by Bourin and Uchiyama, and Kosem, respectively.   In this paper we consider the related question whether the inequalities $||| f(A)-f(B) ||| \le ||| f(|A-B|) |||$, and $||| g(A)-g(B) ||| \ge ||| g(|A-B|) |||$, obtained by Ando, for operator monotone $f$ with inverse $g$, also have a similar generalisation to non-negative concave $f$ and convex $g$. We answer exactly this question, in the negative for general matrices, and affirmatively in the special case when $A\ge ||B||$.   In the course of this work, we introduce the novel notion of $Y$-dominated majorisation between the spectra of two Hermitian matrices, where $Y$ is itself a Hermitian matrix, and prove a certain property of this relation that allows to strengthen the results of Bourin-Uchiyama and Kosem, mentioned above.

outputs.L1:
For positive semidefinite matrices \(A\) and \(B\), Ando and Zhan proved that
\[
|||f(A)+f(B)||| \geq |||f(A+B)|||
\quad\text{and}\quad
|||g(A)+g(B)||| \leq |||g(A+B)|||
\]
for every unitarily invariant norm, where \(f\) is any non-negative operator-monotone function on \([0,\infty)\) and \(g\) is its inverse. These inequalities were recently generalised by Bourin and Uchiyama to non-negative concave functions \(f\), and by Kosem to non-negative convex functions \(g\).

In this paper, we investigate the related question of whether Ando’s inequalities
\[
|||f(A)-f(B)||| \leq |||f(|A-B|)|||
\quad\text{and}\quad
|||g(A)-g(B)||| \geq |||g(|A-B|)|||,
\]
originally established for operator-monotone \(f\) with inverse \(g\), admit analogous generalisations to non-negative concave functions \(f\) and convex functions \(g\). We provide a definitive answer: negative for general matrices, but affirmative in the special case \(A\geq ||B||\).

In the course of this work, we introduce the novel notion of \(Y\)-dominated majorisation between the spectra of two Hermitian matrices, where \(Y\) is itself Hermitian. We establish a property of this relation that enables us to strengthen the aforementioned results of Bourin–Uchiyama and Kosem.
outputs.L2:
Ando and Zhan established that, for positive semidefinite matrices \(A\) and \(B\),
\[
|||f(A)+f(B)|||\geq |||f(A+B)|||
\]
and
\[
|||g(A)+g(B)|||\leq |||g(A+B)|||,
\]
with respect to every unitarily invariant norm, whenever \(f\) is a non-negative operator-monotone function on \([0,\infty)\) and \(g\) is its inverse. More recently, Bourin and Uchiyama extended the first inequality to non-negative concave functions \(f\), while Kosem extended the second to non-negative convex functions \(g\).

This paper examines whether two related inequalities due to Ando,
\[
|||f(A)-f(B)|||\leq |||f(|A-B|)|||
\]
and
\[
|||g(A)-g(B)|||\geq |||g(|A-B|)|||,
\]
which hold for operator-monotone \(f\) and its inverse \(g\), admit analogous extensions to non-negative concave \(f\) and non-negative convex \(g\). We show that such extensions fail for arbitrary matrices but do hold in the special situation \(A\geq ||B||\).

As part of the analysis, we define a new relation called \(Y\)-dominated majorisation between the spectra of two Hermitian matrices, with \(Y\) itself Hermitian. We then establish a property of this relation that yields stronger versions of the aforementioned results of Bourin–Uchiyama and Kosem.
outputs.L3:
Ando and Zhan established norm inequalities for sums of functions of positive semidefinite matrices with respect to arbitrary unitarily invariant norms. Their work was subsequently extended by Bourin and Uchiyama, who proved corresponding sum inequalities for non-negative concave functions, and by Kosem, who obtained analogous results for non-negative convex functions.

The paper examines whether similar inequalities for differences can be generalized beyond operator monotone functions and their inverses to the broader classes of non-negative concave and convex functions. Although such a generalization fails for arbitrary matrices, the authors show that it remains valid under the additional condition \(A \ge \|B\|\), where the scalar \(\|B\|\) is understood as \(\|B\|I\) in the operator inequality.

To develop and refine these results, the authors introduce the concept of \(Y\)-dominated majorisation for the spectra of Hermitian matrices. This new framework not only supports the difference inequalities in the special case above but also yields strengthened versions of the earlier sum inequalities established by Bourin–Uchiyama and Kosem.
outputs.L4:
This paper examines the extent to which Ando’s inequalities for differences of matrix functions remain valid beyond their classical setting. Ando’s results compare \(f(A)-f(B)\) with \(f(|A-B|)\), typically through unitarily invariant norms or spectral majorisation, when \(f\) is a non-negative operator-monotone function; corresponding reverse-type statements arise for inverse functions. A natural question is whether operator monotonicity can be replaced by the weaker scalar assumptions of concavity or convexity.

To address this question, the paper introduces a new notion of \(Y\)-dominated majorisation for the spectra of Hermitian matrices. This framework records spectral information relative to a fixed dominating matrix \(Y\) and is designed to handle differences that need not be positive semidefinite. It provides a unified way to formulate and compare inequalities for concave and convex functional calculus.

The results show that the proposed extensions are false for arbitrary positive semidefinite matrices: non-negativity and scalar concavity, or convexity in the inverse formulation, do not by themselves guarantee the corresponding Ando-type inequalities. However, the inequalities become valid under the additional separation condition
\[
A\geq \|B\|I,
\]
written briefly as \(A\geq \|B\|\). Thus, when the spectrum of \(A\) lies sufficiently far above that of \(B\), the desired majorisation and norm comparisons can be recovered for the broader classes of non-negative concave and convex functions.

In addition, the \(Y\)-dominated majorisation principle yields refinements of known inequalities for matrix functions. In particular, it strengthens earlier results of Bourin–Uchiyama and Kosem by replacing their norm-level conclusions with a more informative spectral comparison. The paper therefore both identifies the limitations of extending Ando’s inequalities and provides a new majorisation tool that gives sharper results under an appropriate ordering hypothesis.
outputs.L5:
**For Ando and Zhan**

For Ando and Zhan, every journey began with curiosity. Ando brought bold ideas and endless energy, while Zhan offered patience and careful thought. Together, they turned obstacles into opportunities and uncertainty into discovery. Their story was a reminder that different strengths, united by trust, can lead to remarkable achievements.

counterfactuals.prompt: Write an abstract for a research paper on extensions of Ando’s matrix norm inequalities from operator monotone functions to non-negative concave and convex functions.
counterfactuals.output: We extend Ando’s matrix norm inequalities, originally established for operator monotone functions, to substantially broader classes of scalar functions. For positive semidefinite matrices and arbitrary unitarily invariant norms, we derive analogues for non-negative concave functions, without assuming operator monotonicity, and obtain complementary inequalities for convex functions satisfying the natural normalization at the origin. Our approach combines eigenvalue majorization, block-matrix techniques, and variational characterizations of symmetric norms, thereby separating the role of scalar convexity or concavity from genuinely operator-theoretic assumptions. The resulting estimates include norm inequalities for sums and differences of matrix functions, recover the classical Ando inequalities as special cases, and yield applications to Schatten norms and trace inequalities. Examples are provided to demonstrate the sharpness of the hypotheses and to clarify the limitations of possible operator-order extensions.
counterfactuals.label: cf_1

counterfactuals.prompt: Summarize a paper investigating whether the inequalities \(|||f(A)-f(B)|||\le |||f(|A-B|)|||\) and \(|||g(A)-g(B)|||\ge |||g(|A-B|)|||\) extend to concave \(f\) and convex \(g\), including the main positive and negative results.
counterfactuals.output:
The paper considers positive semidefinite matrices \(A,B\) and unitarily invariant norms \(|||\cdot|||\). It asks whether the familiar operator-monotone estimate  
\[
|||f(A)-f(B)|||\le |||f(|A-B|)|||
\]
remains valid when \(f\colon[0,\infty)\to[0,\infty)\), \(f(0)=0\), is merely concave, and whether the reverse estimate  
\[
|||g(A)-g(B)|||\ge |||g(|A-B|)|||
\]
holds for nonnegative convex \(g\) with \(g(0)=0\).

The main conclusions are:

- **Positive result:** Both inequalities are valid for the Hilbert–Schmidt/Frobenius norm. Equivalently,
  \[
  \operatorname{Tr}|f(A)-f(B)|^{2}\le
  \operatorname{Tr} f(|A-B|)^{2},
  \]
  with the inequality reversed for convex \(g\). This gives a broad extension beyond operator-monotone or operator-convex functions at the level of the \(2\)-norm. The commuting case also reduces to the corresponding scalar inequalities.

- **Negative result:** Scalar concavity or convexity alone is not sufficient for arbitrary unitarily invariant norms. The paper constructs finite-dimensional, noncommuting counterexamples showing that the proposed inequalities fail for standard unitarily invariant norms outside the Hilbert–Schmidt setting. Thus one cannot simply replace “operator monotone” by “concave,” nor expect the convex reverse inequality in full norm generality.

Overall, the paper identifies the Frobenius norm as a robust positive case while showing that the stronger all-unitarily-invariant-norm formulations require genuinely operator-theoretic hypotheses, not just ordinary scalar concavity or convexity.
counterfactuals.label: cf_2

counterfactuals.prompt: Draft a mathematical abstract explaining how the work of Ando–Zhan, Bourin–Uchiyama, and Kosem motivates a study of difference inequalities for positive semidefinite matrices and unitarily invariant norms.
counterfactuals.output:
**Abstract.** Classical results of Ando–Zhan, Bourin–Uchiyama, and Kosem show that scalar monotonicity and concavity can persist, in norm form, for nonlinear functions of positive semidefinite matrices. In particular, their work establishes subadditivity-type inequalities for unitarily invariant norms, comparing \(f(A+B)\) with \(f(A)+f(B)\), and suggests corresponding perturbation estimates comparing \(f(A)-f(B)\) with \(f(|A-B|)\). Motivated by this circle of ideas, we study difference inequalities of the form
\[
\|f(A)-f(B)\|_{\!u}\leq \|f(|A-B|)\|_{\!u},
\]
and related weak-majorization statements, where \(A,B\geq0\), \(f:[0,\infty)\to[0,\infty)\) is increasing and concave with \(f(0)=0\), and \(\|\cdot\|_{\!u}\) is an arbitrary unitarily invariant norm. We examine how such estimates arise from matrix subadditivity, spectral comparison, and singular-value inequalities, and identify the hypotheses under which scalar modulus-of-continuity bounds admit noncommutative analogues. The resulting framework connects sum inequalities with stability estimates for matrix functional calculus and clarifies the role of positivity, concavity, and unitary invariance in controlling nonlinear matrix differences.
counterfactuals.label: cf_3

counterfactuals.prompt: Provide a concise research overview of new results on norm inequalities for matrix functions, emphasizing the special case \(A\ge \|B\|\) and the introduction of \(Y\)-dominated majorisation.
counterfactuals.output:
Recent work on norm inequalities for matrix functions develops perturbation and comparison bounds beyond the usual operator-monotone or globally concave settings.

- **Dominant-background case.** A particularly tractable regime is
  \[
  A\ge \|B\|I,
  \]
  often abbreviated \(A\ge\|B\|\). Here \(A\) is positive and dominates the perturbation \(B\) in operator norm, so \(A\pm B\ge0\) when \(B\) is Hermitian. This spectral separation permits sharper inequalities for expressions involving \(f(A\pm B)\), differences of matrix functions, and related block matrices. The resulting estimates typically hold for broad classes of unitarily invariant norms and require weaker assumptions on \(f\) than comparable unrestricted results.

- **Proof mechanism.** The condition allows the relevant matrices to be embedded into positive \(2\times2\) block matrices. Positivity, unitary-orbit decompositions, and Ky Fan norm estimates then reduce nonlinear matrix inequalities to controlled eigenvalue or singular-value comparisons.

- **\(Y\)-dominated majorisation.** The work introduces a relative form of majorisation in which the comparison is made under the control of a fixed positive matrix \(Y\). Rather than demanding ordinary majorisation—which can be too strong—the new relation records precisely the partial-sum or symmetric-norm domination available from the block-matrix argument. It is strong enough to imply the desired unitarily invariant norm inequalities but flexible enough to accommodate noncommuting matrices.

- **Significance.** The framework separates two issues: structural domination supplied by \(A\ge\|B\|I\), and functional assumptions on \(f\). It therefore clarifies why certain scalar-looking norm inequalities survive noncommutativity in the dominated regime, while corresponding unrestricted Loewner-order or eigenvalue-majorisation statements may fail. \(Y\)-dominated majorisation also provides a reusable intermediate tool for future inequalities involving matrix functions, perturbations, and positive block matrices.
counterfactuals.label: cf_4

counterfactuals.prompt: Compose an academic-style abstract for a matrix analysis paper that answers whether Ando’s operator-monotone difference inequalities generalize to non-negative concave and convex functions, and mention any new spectral majorization concept developed in the proof.
counterfactuals.output:
We extend Ando’s difference inequality from operator-monotone functions to the broader classes of scalar concave and convex functions. For positive semidefinite matrices \(A,B\) and every non-negative concave function \(f\) on \([0,\infty)\), we prove the weak majorization
\[
s\!\left(f(A)-f(B)\right)\prec_w s\!\left(f(|A-B|)\right),
\]
and hence the corresponding inequality for every unitarily invariant norm. For non-negative convex functions satisfying \(f(0)=0\), we establish the complementary reverse-type majorization, thereby showing that operator monotonicity is not essential once the direction of comparison is adapted to curvature. The proof develops a spectral-spread majorization, an order based on paired gaps between the largest and smallest eigenvalues of a Hermitian matrix. This new spectral majorization framework provides the eigenvalue control needed for the convex case and may be useful independently in perturbation theory and nonlinear matrix inequalities.
counterfactuals.label: cf_5
